paper.title: Dense Language Generation Made Simple: Deterministic, Randomized, and Multi-Order Algorithms
paper.summary: Develops the patient-scope method for deterministic dense generation and extends the framework to randomized and simultaneous multi-order guarantees. This registry keeps the earlier manuscript and public arXiv v1 mathematically separate because Definition 3.2 changed between them; it also records public-v1 randomized and multi-order headline theorems even though those results have no P39 Lean formalization.

formalization_scope.summary: The custom inventory contains twenty edition-specific claims: eight from the earlier supplied manuscript and twelve from public arXiv v1. Lean fully covers six earlier-manuscript claims and the isolated public-v1 criticality definition, partially covers earlier Fact 3.12 and Theorem 3.14, and covers none of the other eleven public-v1 claims. In particular, the existing P39 patient-scope machine uses the earlier recursive-criticality interface and does not formalize any public-v1 algorithm theorem.
specializations: The P39 machine's RecursiveCritical predicate compares a candidate only with earlier recursively critical candidates, exactly as in the earlier manuscript; public-v1 Definition 3.2 instead compares with every earlier consistent candidate.

The isolated public-v1 Definition 3.2 is represented by GenLimit.Critical from the P01 semantic development, but that cross-paper definition link does not connect the existing P39 machine or any P39 algorithm theorem to public v1.
Paper indices and positive integers are translated to zero-based natural-number indices and Finset.range prefixes.
The Lean algorithms are semantic and noncomputable: whole-language inclusion, infinitude filtering, and closure reindexing are not realized by finite membership queries.
The Example 3.15 counterexample is witnessed by the explicit increasing enumeration 4, 8, 12, and so on; the source specifies the enumerated set but does not print an enumeration order.
The density theorems use target-relative prefix counts, so the target need not equal the whole ambient universe.
gaps: The earlier Theorem 3.14 optimality upper bound is not formalized; only the patient-scope 1/2 achievability result is maintained in Lean.

Earlier Fact 3.12 has a maintained strict previous-output comparison, but its preceding-focus membership is not exposed as a standalone paper-facing declaration; the derived predecessor-pairing declarations are non-covering proof support.
No public-v1 patient-scope theorem is formalized because the strengthened Definition 3.2 changes the criticality interface on which the machine and its invariants depend.
The randomized 1 - 1/e lower and upper bounds and the deterministic and randomized multi-order algorithms are source-only.

Public Lemma 3.18 has an insufficient candidate-subset step in its printed proof under public-v1 criticality. Its conclusion appears repairable, but neither the repair nor the resulting Theorem 3.19 proof is formalized.
The historical human audit of the earlier-manuscript Theorem 3.14 predates a wrapper cleanup; a narrow re-audit of the current wrapper remains pending.
Definitions and support results outside the two declared custom source scopes, proof-only helpers, appendices, and weaker recap theorems are not independently carded.

relations.notes: Public v1 changes Definition 3.2 from comparison with earlier recursively critical languages to comparison with every earlier consistent language and renumbers the partial-enumeration results.

This public revision strengthens the criticality interface, adds Remarks 3.15--3.16, renumbers the partial-enumeration items, and is the edition used for the registered randomized and multi-order headline claims.

claims.title: Earlier-manuscript counterexample to direct patient-scope under partial enumeration
claims.statement_summary: For a family whose first language contains the positive odds and multiples of four and whose true second language is the positive evens, an adversary enumerating only multiples of four can keep the first language as the sole critical language, causing direct patient-scope to output only odds and fail generation in the limit.

source_assessment.notes: The source fixes the enumerated set but does not print an enumeration order. Lean supplies the explicit increasing order 4, 8, 12, and so on, which is a valid witness to the counterexample.

formalization.notes: An explicit increasing enumeration of the paper's enumerated set witnesses every claimed behavior and the resulting failure of validity.

components.summary: The stream 4, 8, 12, and so on exactly presents the multiples of four.
The direct patient-scope machine outputs the positive odd numbers in order.
Every machine output lies outside the true language of positive even numbers.

lean_links.notes: Fixes the enumeration order omitted by the prose example.
Exact operational behavior for the chosen legal enumeration.

claims.title: Earlier-manuscript finite-intersection closure restores partial-enumeration validity
claims.statement_summary: If an infinite enumerated set E is contained in a true language K, then patient-scope run on the filtered family of nonempty finite intersections eventually generates fresh elements of K.

source_assessment.notes: The semantic conclusion is clear. The source's discussion of discarding finite intersections and reindexing does not by itself give an effective infinitude test; Lean represents this filtering classically and noncomputably.

formalization.notes: The paper-shaped endpoint includes eventual target membership, freshness from all data seen so far, and nonrepetition for the closure patient-scope run. It makes no effective infinitude-filter claim.

lean_links.notes: Uniform in the family, target index, infinite E, and presentation, with only E subset K supplied to the generator proof.

The conclusion appears repairable, for example via a suitable maximal-consistent closure candidate, but that repair is not printed or formalized. Infinitude filtering and reindexing are also semantic rather than effective.
